newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS SAYS TO LAUNCH DVD IN THE SPRING.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS SAYS TO LAUNCH DVD IN THE SPRING.

text.p: Philips Electronics said on Tuesday it planned to launch a Digital Video Disc (DVD) player in the U.S. for around $600 in the spring.
Jan Oosterveld, president of Philips Key Modules unit, made the announcement during a briefing to journalists ahead of the CeBIT trade fair in Germany next month.

He was updating a previous statement that Philips would probably launch DVD players in the U.S. at the beginning of 1997 for between $500 and $800. Philips is to launch two models in Europe early in September for between 1,500 and 1,800 guilders, Oosterveld added.

Pioneer Electronic Corp last week shipped the first of its DVD players to high-end U.S. retailers at a suggested retail price of $1,750, and is expected to launch two players in the spring at $999 and $599.
Toshiba is expected to begin shipping players in late March or April in the $600 price range, while Sony is to introduce a DVD player this spring for around $1,000.

"We expect the first buyers to be home cinema enthusiasts," said Oosterveld. "Looking at the announcements from the movie industry, we are confident that the number of titles available at launch is sufficient to attract the first buyers."
DVD technology allows huge amounts of information to be stored on a compact disc (CD), such as high quality images, sound and data. One DVD disc can hold as much information as 12 CD-ROM discs.
Hardware companies from Japan, Europe and the U.S. have agreed on a single standard technology, but worries about home copying and piracy have held up introduction of DVD.
"We consider DVD a successful format in the the future with expected sales of around 25 to 30 million in the 2000," said Oosterveld. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
